scope: Employment lifecycle, server-filtered staff reads and collaboration ownership
summary: Former-staff history is limited to current staff administrators. Shared active-staff reads use an authenticated gateway; direct collection reads and cross-staff edits are restricted. Emulator and fixture checks cover normal collaboration flows.

findings.issue: Cached administrator/HR claims and stale permission mirrors could retain grants after profile changes.
findings.recommendation: Implemented: authorize from the current staff profile in Firestore rules and protected server APIs.

findings.issue: Direct client employment and credential changes could bypass lifecycle or password endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Implemented: server-only update fields, active-only client account creation, create/update profile validators, and blocked legacy-inactive transitions.

findings.issue: Employment notes and employment audit entries require distinct read/write controls.
findings.recommendation: Implemented: current full/users admins can read notes, server-only note writes, and immutable server-written employment audit entries.

findings.issue: Shared collection queries include historical records. Database-confidential former-staff archives cannot be enforced merely by hiding rows in the client.
findings.recommendation: Implemented authenticated paginated gateway plus direct-read rules. All active staff remain visible to active staff; former and orphan personal history require a current administrator.

findings.issue: Other legacy collaboration collections permit broad authenticated writes; this targeted employment change does not certify their ownership controls.
findings.recommendation: Implemented owner/field rules, authenticated minutes and task handoff endpoints, private-parent validation, and admin-only shared-ranking writes.

findings.issue: Unrelated legacy documents and arrays have no comprehensive app-wide size constraints.
findings.recommendation: Introduce collection-specific validators with migration-compatible limits in a separate compatibility-tested pass.
